findings.title: The hand-over picker names a killer the opening veils: a victim or a bystander in the room presses Give and reads the killer's name in the list
findings.where: scripts/handover.mjs:46-69 (askWhoIsHere: the list is othersInRoom, each named by nameAsSeen); scripts/movement.mjs:3761-3772, 3781-3785, 3808-3816 (countsAsPresent keeps a veiled token); scripts/mask-gm.mjs:120-124, 154-158 (nameAsSeen masks only a masked actor); scripts/visibility.mjs:555-561 (the veil hides the token); scripts/allowed-now.mjs:107-108
findings.what_happens: While a direct murder waits on its opening, the killer's token carries the veil flag and every browser but the killer's side's and the GMs' hides it (visibility.mjs tokenShownTo). The veil writes no `hidden` since E112v, and countsAsPresent reads only `hidden` (utils.mjs hiddenByGm), so on the victim's or a bystander's own browser othersInRoom lists the killer. askWhoIsHere asks the client gate first, whose handover road shuts only for an Eclipse (allowed-now.mjs:108), and draws each option with nameAsSeen, which hides a name only behind a mask (isMaskedActor reads the `masked` flag, not `veiled`). The picker therefore shows the killer's real name to a player whose screen shows no killer. The GM's side refuses the give itself (inventory.mjs transferRefusal, the giver's incident), but the list has already been drawn. The same window serves the sheet's Give / Share buttons (sheet-inventory.mjs:988-1013), Show the passage (sheet-sidebar.mjs:644-655) and game.drpg.giveItemDialog (api.mjs:777).
findings.failure_scenario: Aiko's player, the victim, sees nobody else in the Library while the killer's opening waits; she presses Give on her notebook, and the window offers 'Botan Kage' - the killer her screen hides, and whom a Hope opening would then put behind a '?'.
findings.expected: A list of who is here names a veiled character as it names a masked one ("?") to a player who does not own it, or leaves it out of the list on that player's browser, while the veil stands; the veil's own note (mask-gm.mjs:358-362) says the killer is 'hidden from every player but the killer's side, bystanders included'.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a gate that keeps the window shut during an incident: the client gate is the Eclipse alone (allowed-now.mjs:108), rowGate keys on the sheet's mode, not the incident (sheet-mode.mjs:135-137), and transferRefusal runs on the GM after the list is drawn (inventory.mjs:1095-1098). Looked for the veil in the names: nameAsSeen and isMaskedActor read `masked` only (mask-gm.mjs:115-124); R7404 holds the masked case and names handover.mjs among its files (R-REGISTRY.md:1702), and the veil's design table (docs/dev/e112v/DESIGN.md section 1) lists the token, ruler, silhouette, voice and nameplate but no picker. Counting the killer in the room is a decision (R7705); naming them in a list is not covered by it. Not run: no probe or harness read of the picker during a veil.
findings.live_check: One GM, the killer's player, the victim's player: open a direct murder in daylight, and while the opening waits press Give on an item on the victim's sheet; the list should not show the killer's name.

findings.title: Room Setup lists every named region, and a name that no piece can make a room keeps its owner, locks, table, description, picture and stash cells live while Apply writes none of them
findings.where: scripts/room-setup.mjs:948-955 (namedByName sets the name before the canBeRoom test), 1240 (rows from its keys), 297-299, 310-311, 318-320 (only This is a room and the actions drawn off), 984-985 (Apply skips the row)
findings.what_happens: namedByName puts every region name in the map and pushes only the pieces that can be rooms, so a name only a Teleport, a level change or a player's region carries is a row with no pieces. roomCells draws that row with This is a room and the room's actions disabled, and every other cell - owner, Locked, Locked at start, Broken, No privacy, Neighbours, No search, the item table, the place switches, the description, the picture, the stash cells - as live controls. applyRoomRows `continue`s on such a row before comparing anything, applyStashMatrix's setStash writes nothing for it, and nothing is said. Its Fog boxes, Discover all included, do write discovery cells for a name that is no room (fog.mjs:1541-1553), and its stepper writes a counter at once (search-tokens.mjs:366-382). The hint on the disabled switch explains the switch only (DRPG.Vault.isRoomHint).
findings.failure_scenario: A GM names the staircase's level-change region 'Stairwell', opens Room Setup, types a description and ticks Locked on the Stairwell row, presses Apply, and is told rooms were applied; on reopen the row is blank again with no word why.
findings.expected: A name that no piece can make a room is drawn with its cells off (or not drawn outside the Rooms tab), and Apply says when a row it was given wrote nothing.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a notice or a disabled state on the other cells: none in roomCells (204-376) or readRoomSetupForm (532-587); bedroomClaimedTwice counts such a row's owner too (894-908). The header of namedByName (941-947) says such a name has no pieces and so nothing a row may write - by design for Apply, but the cells are not drawn to match. Not covered by controls-11-map-rooms-3, which is about a marked-later room's actions.

findings.title: Every room's search count this time of day is a world setting every browser holds: a console reads which rooms somebody searched, and how often, in rooms the player was never in
findings.where: scripts/settings.mjs:3433-3440 (searchTokens, scope world); scripts/search-tokens.mjs:7-10, 92-95, 334-346; scripts/world-secrets.mjs:67-110 (no rule names it; eclipseMoves 84-87 for the like case)
findings.what_happens: The counters are `{ "<sceneId>::<room>": left }`, written by the primary on every spend and absent for a full room. Foundry sends world settings to every client, so `game.settings.get("danganronpa-rpg", "searchTokens")` on a player's console lists every room on every scene that was searched since the last refill, and how many times. The interface shows a player only their own room's count (room-tile.mjs:168), and the room rule hides who stands where (visibility.mjs). The Eclipse's crossings - who moved how often - were taken out of world data for the same kind of fact (E05 C4, world-secrets.mjs:84-87; gm-stores.mjs:1325-1337); the search counts were not, and no rule or note says they are public.
findings.failure_scenario: During Daily Life a player types one line in the console and sees the Kitchen at 1 of 3 and the Storage room at 2 of 3 on a floor they have not visited - somebody went through both this afternoon - before any body is found.
findings.expected: Either the counts are the GMs' (a store, with each player's copy holding the rooms their characters stand in), or the owner records that the counts are public, as the overflow's stamp is (world-secrets.mjs:93).
findings.refutation_tried: Searched docs/ and scripts/ for a decision that the counts are public (grep for searchTokens with public / every browser): none. WORLD_SECRET_RULES has no row for it, so R9, R190 and 72-canary do not hold it. The value names no character, which is why this is minor and not major: it tells activity in a room, not who.

findings.title: A readiness round left open by a GM who disconnected is ended 'stop' during an incident by the next GM's press, and every player it asked is told 'The GM is waiting a little longer'
findings.where: scripts/boundary.mjs:336-354 (openRoundOnPrimary: `cleared` writes ended 'stop' before roundAllowed is asked), 551-558 (renderReadyRound tells a player of a 'stop'); against 47-62 (E37 fix FG1b and FG1c)
findings.what_happens: openRoundOnPrimary computes `cleared` - an open round whose GM is not connected - and sets `write = { ...open, ended: "stop" }` before it asks roundAllowed, then writes it whatever roundAllowed answers. On every player's browser that showed that round's window, renderReadyRound reads ended 'stop' and posts DRPG.Ready.cancelled. With an incident running before Stage 6, the press that reaches this is 'Next time of day' (nextTimeOfDay asks no incident first; toggleEclipse's start is refused by startRefusal), so the line lands at the moment a GM moves the hidden clock. FG1b and FG1c took exactly this out of the incident's start and of a barred 'go' because 'every player of the round was told ... that the GM was waiting a little longer: a timing signal to the bystanders'.
findings.failure_scenario: GM A asks the players before Next time of day and drops off; a murder opens in the Gym; GM B presses Next time of day, and every bystander whose round window was still up sees 'The GM is waiting a little longer' at that moment, though their clock shows nothing moving.
findings.expected: While a round may not run (roundAllowed false), a round cleared for a gone GM is written as FG1c writes a barred one - 'go', nothing told - or left to go stale with the clock.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the path is reachable during an incident: nextTimeOfDay refuses only an Eclipse (134-139) and askReadiness asks the primary (455-461); the incident's start writes nothing to the round (FG1b), so an open round can stand into an incident; roundOf keeps it open while the clock stays at its boundary (261-266). A player who had said Done still has shownFor set and is told. Rare: it needs the round's GM gone. Not run.

findings.title: The search counters' queue holds on one browser only: a refill or Room Setup's step written by a GM who is not the primary can write over a spend the primary wrote a moment before, or bring one back
findings.where: scripts/search-tokens.mjs:366-382 (setFor), 396-401 (reset), 329-349 (#spendAsGm), 435-439 and 503-509 (the notes); scripts/utils.mjs:409-415 (serialWrite); scripts/clock.mjs:377, 815 (the refill on the GM who moves the clock)
findings.what_happens: Every write of the counters reads and writes the whole object in a step of SEARCH_KEY, and serialWrite is an in-memory queue of this browser. A player's spend is run on the primary; a time of day's refill (`SearchTokens.reset` from advanceTimeOfDay) and Room Setup's stepper (`setFor`) run on whichever GM pressed. Two writes from two browsers inside one server round trip each start from the copy their browser holds: the primary's spend written after a non-primary GM's refill puts back every room's pre-refill counts less one, and Room Setup's step on another GM writes the whole store as that GM last saw it over a spend in another room. The note at 435-439 credits the step with closing the reset's race, which it does only for the season reset (on the primary).
findings.failure_scenario: An Assistant GM presses Next time of day as a player's Search in the Library is spent on the primary; the refill lands first and the spend's step then writes the old counts back, so the new afternoon opens with yesterday's searched-out rooms still at 0.
findings.expected: Every write of the counters goes through the primary's queue (a bridge row or the GM store), as a player's spend already does.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a primary check in reset and setFor: none (396-401, 366-382); giveBack and the bridge spend check isPrimaryGm in the step (308, 333). advanceTimeOfDay is gated on isGM, not on the primary (clock.mjs:377). The window is one round trip, so this is a nit; not measured.

findings.title: Room Setup probes every room picture at once on each open, one probe per room rather than per path, which Pre-season checks was changed not to do
findings.where: scripts/room-setup.mjs:773-790 (wirePictureWarnings), 1333; against scripts/room-tile.mjs:650-655, 664-689 (checkRoomImages: each path once, ROOM_IMAGE_LIMITS.atOnce at a time)
findings.what_happens: wirePictureWarnings calls imageFacts - a full decode and a HEAD - for every picture cell as the window opens, all together and once per room even where rooms share a path. checkRoomImages, which reads the same facts for Pre-season checks, was changed in E20's fix round to probe each path once and a few at a time, because probing a school's eighteen pictures together on one connection read them all as missing. A late probe here says nothing (pictureWarning gives no line for `late`), so the cost is traffic and decode work at each open, not a wrong warning.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM on a slow line opens Room Setup on a school of eighteen 3 MB pictures to tick one lock, and the browser fetches and decodes all eighteen before anything else loads.
findings.expected: The cells read their facts through the same bounded, per-path probe Pre-season checks uses, or only when the Description tab is shown.
findings.refutation_tried: The browser's cache may answer repeat paths; whether Foundry's server sends cache headers for module or world files is not read here. Not measured.

findings.title: Room Setup's held Apply puts a student's name into Foundry's tooltip through an empty data-tooltip and the aria-label, the road R4764 and the room tile's header say not to take
findings.where: scripts/room-setup.mjs:871-886 (setApplyBlock), 840-849 (the reason, `DRPG.Vault.twoRooms` with the actor's and the rooms' names unescaped); scripts/room-tile.mjs:28-30; docs/dev/R-REGISTRY.md:1432 (R4764)
findings.what_happens: While one student is given two bedrooms, setApplyBlock sets `data-tooltip=""` and the reason as the button's aria-label. R4764's row and room-tile.mjs say Foundry then reads the aria-label through the client's cleanHTML as the tooltip's markup (the E02-D01 hole). The reason is game.i18n.format with the student's name - which the owning player may set - and two region names, none escaped. What cleanHTML leaves of markup in a name is Foundry's code, not read here.
findings.failure_scenario: A player renames their student with markup in it; the GM gives that student a second bedroom in Room Setup and hovers the greyed Apply, and the tooltip draws the name as markup rather than as text.
findings.expected: The reason as a tooltip in text form (setTip's `text: true`, data-tooltip-text), as R4764 asks of a tooltip written in code.
findings.refutation_tried: Read R4764's row: it holds the six controls made in code and the two tiles; setApplyBlock writes its attribute by hand and is not among them. Whether cleanHTML keeps any visible markup, and whether a player's actor name reaches the GM unescaped elsewhere, was not read in Foundry's source. A question, not a finding, until a table reads it.

A Mastermind standing in the lair sees the whole cast, Remnants excepted.
A Spectator's browser leaves every character to Foundry, the veiled killer excepted.

Every student's token wears a frame on every screen, the viewer's own in bone; a missing frame on the Mastermind would be the tell.

l1.what: The names the hand-over window lists while the opening veils the killer.
recipe: Start a world with a GM, the killer's player and the victim's player, room visibility on.
Put the killer and the victim in one room in Daily Life and open a direct murder; do not throw the opening roll.
On the victim's browser open the victim's sheet and press Give on any item.
Read the names in the 'Who' list.
Repeat with Share on a Truth Bullet and with 'Show the passage' if the victim knows one.
l1.settles_if: The list names the killer: finding 1 holds. The list names nobody or '?': it does not.

not_established.what: Whether two students standing outside every room (a corridor) should see each other wherever they are on the map, and whether a player viewing a scene where they have no token should see every character outside the rooms.
not_established.why: visibility.mjs:614 answers null (Foundry's own visibility) whenever the viewer stands in no room and the token stands in none; the comment names only a scene with no regions. The guide's line ('Players see other players only in the same room') does not settle corridors, and I found no decision on it.

l1.what: The greyed Apply's tooltip when the clashing student's name holds markup.
recipe: As a player, rename an owned student to a name with simple markup, e.g. a bold tag around it.
As GM open Room Setup, Rooms tab, and give that student two bedrooms.
Read whether the name shows as text or as formatting.
l1.settles_if: Formatting shows: finding 7 holds. The tags show as text: it does not.

not_established.what: Whether own-ring.mjs's refreshToken listener runs before or after visibility.mjs's on v14.
not_established.why: Either order leaves the frame hidden with the token, since the frame is the token's child (own-ring.mjs:285-297) and hide() writes token.visible false (visibility.mjs:871-874); the order only decides whether a hidden token's frame is rebuilt or kept. No table reading; not a finding either way.

not_established.live_check: game.drpg.fps({ toChat: false }) during a drag on a scene with many regions, as LIVE-E88-01 reads the table

l1.what: Frame time during a token's drag on a scene of many rooms, with the module's counters.
recipe: Open a scene with 20 or more room regions.
As a player, drag your token across three rooms while `await game.drpg.fps({ toChat: false })` runs.
Read the frame rate and visibility.sliding in the report.
l1.settles_if: Frames over 33 ms grow with the region count: worth a finding. Flat: nothing to say.
